topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: HarborWorks schedules work by urgency. It does not need the complete queue sorted after every arrival; it needs the next most urgent item quickly. Maintaining more order than the operation requires can waste work. A heap preserves exactly enough structure to expose one extreme element while supporting efficient updates.

topics.summary: In a zero-based array, the children of index p are 2p+1 and 2p+2 when those indices exist. The parent of a nonroot index i is (i-1)/2. topics.title: 12.1.2 Performing Heapify Operations
topics.summary: Sifting down assumes both child subtrees are already heaps and only the current root may violate their order. Choose the smaller existing child. If that child is not smaller than the parent, stop; otherwise exchange them and repeat at the child’s former index. Choosing an arbitrary child can leave a smaller sibling above an incorrectly placed value.

blocks.text: Bottom-up heap construction starts at the last internal node and sifts each internal node down toward the root. Leaves need no work. This construction takes O(n), not O(n log n): most nodes are close to leaves and can move only a short distance. Summing work over levels gives a bound proportional to n times a convergent series of h/2^h.

blocks.text: Sift-down begins with a precise assumption: both child subtrees are already heaps, and only the current root may violate their order. Compare the existing children and select the smaller one. If that child is not smaller than the parent, the whole local subtree is a heap. Otherwise swap and continue at the child position.

If that child is not smaller than the parent, the whole local subtree is a heap. Otherwise swap and continue at the child position.

blocks.text: Choosing the smaller child is necessary. Suppose a parent has value nine and children four and two. Swapping with four leaves two smaller than the new parent four, so the parent-child invariant is still broken. The repair must satisfy both child relationships, not merely improve one comparison.

blocks.text: Bottom-up construction starts from the final internal node and moves toward the root. Leaves already satisfy heap order. When an internal node is processed, its children have been processed or are leaves, so sift-down’s precondition holds. This is a dependency-ordered algorithm much like postorder aggregation in a tree.

blocks.text: The construction’s linear bound is subtler than multiplying n by a maximum height. Many nodes are leaves and need no sift; many others can move only one level. Only a small number near the root can travel far. Summing the work by possible height yields a linear total because the number of nodes decreases geometrically as possible travel distance increases.

topics.title: 12.2.1 Inserting Prioritized Values
topics.summary: Insertion appends the new value at the next complete-tree position. Every old parent-child relationship remains valid except possibly the new value’s relationship with its parent. Sift upward while the child is smaller, exchanging with its parent until the rule holds or the root is reached. Each exchange moves up one level, giving O(log n) comparisons in the worst case.

Do not confuse heap-order complexity with all storage-management costs.

blocks.text: Mutable priorities require an update mechanism. Changing a value through a retained pointer bypasses sift repair and can invalidate the heap. A design can provide indexed updates, remove and reinsert entries, or use immutable queued records with stale-entry filtering. The routing capstone later uses the last strategy for tentative distances.

reading.title: 12.2.1 Inserting Prioritized Values
paragraphs: Insertion appends the new value at the next complete-tree position. Every old parent-child relationship remains valid except possibly the new value’s relationship with its parent. Sift upward while the child is smaller, exchanging with its parent until the rule holds or the root is reached. Each exchange moves up one level, giving O(log n) comparisons in the worst case.

Vector growth can occasionally relocate the backing array. The sift work is logarithmic, but a particular append may also incur O(n) relocation. With geometric vector growth, the allocation component is amortized; reserve storage ahead of time when a capacity plan justifies it. Do not confuse heap-order complexity with all storage-management costs.

The teaching class contains integers, for which comparisons and swaps do not throw. A generic heap must address exceptions from comparison, movement, and allocation. It must also define whether an exception leaves heap order preserved, merely leaves objects valid, or requires rebuilding.

Insertion first preserves complete-tree shape by appending at the next array position. Every preexisting parent-child relationship remains unchanged. Only the new value’s relationship with its parent may violate order, so repair follows that one ancestor chain upward.

At each step, compare the child with its parent. If the child is not smaller, stop. Otherwise exchange them and continue from the parent position. The number of possible exchanges is bounded by the complete tree’s height. The proof depends on the appended position and unchanged sibling subtrees, not on a global sort after every insertion.

Storage management remains a separate cost. Vector append may allocate and relocate existing elements when capacity is exhausted. The sift itself has logarithmic comparison work, while a particular storage expansion can cost linear movement. An amortized storage argument explains long-run behavior but does not eliminate a single pause. Reserve when a justified capacity plan is part of the application contract.

A scheduler needs more than an integer priority. If equal priorities must preserve arrival order, compare a pair containing priority and a sequence number under a documented direction. The sequence number must have an overflow policy. A default heap does not promise stable equal-priority ordering merely because one small run happened to preserve it.

Mutable priorities require an update mechanism. Changing a value through a retained pointer bypasses sift repair and can invalidate the heap. A design can provide indexed updates, remove and reinsert entries, or use immutable queued records with stale-entry filtering. The routing capstone later uses the last strategy for tentative distances.

blocks.text: Review reasoning. Why is heap storage not sorted? Only ancestor-child order is maintained. Why choose the smaller child in a minimum heap? The repaired parent must be no greater than both children. Why is bottom-up construction linear? Most nodes have little possible downward travel. Why can one push still relocate many values? The vector’s storage policy is separate from sift complexity. Why does stable priority need extra state? Equal priority alone does not encode arrival order.
